sections.markdown:
## C — The basics, part two: left, U, multi-lane and Y-turns, passing and lane changes, backing, parking on level ground and hills, parallel parking, horn, lights and signals
Knowledge domain: the maneuvers the Wisconsin knowledge test and skills test both draw on — how to turn, when and how to pass, how to back up and park safely, and how to tell other road users what you are about to do with the horn, lights and signals.

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
Before any turn, check your mirrors, your surroundings and your blind spot, stay in your lane, signal your turn and yield the right-of-way. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
Last-second changes of plan are unsafe and can cause a crash, so check mirrors and the traffic behind you before turning into a side road or driveway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
Do not change lanes in the middle of a turn or cut across the center line, and leave extra room for trucks and buses, which may swing over the center line as they turn. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
For a left turn, check that your path is clear, keep near the center line, watch for pedestrians crossing on the left, and wait about halfway into the intersection while leaving room for oncoming turners. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A01
While waiting to turn left, keep the steering wheel and wheels straight, because if you are hit from behind with the wheel turned left you will be pushed into oncoming traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A02
A U-turn is one smooth U-shaped motion that reverses your direction, and it can be very dangerous even though some intersections allow it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A02
Before a U-turn, check all mirrors and traffic and look for any sign that prohibits it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A02
On any rural two-lane highway a U-turn is allowed as long as it is done safely and does not interfere with traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A03
With multiple turn lanes, finish the turn in the matching lane: start in the left-most lane and end in the left-most lane, start in the middle and end in the middle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A03
When turning right from a four-lane roadway, the turn must be made from the lane closest to the right curb or road edge. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A04
Use a Y-turn only in residential areas on streets too narrow for a U-turn; you will also be asked to perform one on the driving exam. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A04
Y-turn step one: signal right, check your mirrors and the traffic on your right, move over as far to the right as possible, and stop. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A04
Y-turn step two is to signal left, check your blind spot, turn left across to the opposite curb and stop. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A04
Y-turn step three is to look back over your right shoulder and reverse just far enough to drive forward again, then stop; step four is to check left and right and pull forward into your lane. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A04
You may use a paved shoulder to get around a vehicle only when that vehicle is stopped or is making a left turn. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A04
On a multi-lane road the left-most lane is the lane for going around slower vehicles, and passing on the right is risky because the other driver may not see you. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A04
If another driver is trying to pass you, keep to your lane and slow down. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A04
Before changing lanes, make sure the way is clear, signal first, move only one lane at a time, and look over the shoulder on the side you are moving toward. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A04
The areas you check over your left and right shoulders are blind spots, which cannot be seen by using your mirrors alone. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A05
Pass only one vehicle at a time and only on the left, since there may not be time to get around several vehicles or even the one ahead of you. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A05
Do not linger in the passing lane, and never exceed the speed limit to complete a pass. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A05
Pass only when there is enough room in front of the vehicle you are passing, and remember that other drivers are not required to move over for you. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A05
It is safe to return to the driving lane once both headlights of the vehicle you passed appear in your rearview mirror. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A05
Because it is hard to see behind a vehicle, back up as little as possible and no faster than a slow walk. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A05
When backing, do not rely only on your mirrors and backup camera: turn your body, look over your right shoulder through the rear window, and use a helper outside the car when you can. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A05
After backing, scan left and right before rejoining traffic, and if you miss an exit or turn, never back up; continue to the next exit and come back. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A05
You are responsible for making sure your parked vehicle is not a hazard, which normally means parking on the far-right side, clear of any travel lane. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A05
Parking is not allowed along yellow-marked curbs, in front of fire hydrants, or where a No Parking sign is posted. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A05
Park at a very low speed, and on level ground shift into Park, or into gear with a manual transmission, and set the parking brake. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A06
Parked uphill with a curb, turn the wheels all the way to the left before shifting into park. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A06
Parked uphill without a curb, turn the wheels all the way to the right before shifting into park. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F32 | anchor: A06
Parked downhill, turn the wheels all the way to the right, and on any hill set the emergency brake. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F33 | anchor: A06
For parallel parking between vehicles, watch for traffic, pedestrians and fixed objects, and look for a space about 3-6 feet longer than your vehicle. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F34 | anchor: A06
Parallel parking starts with your turn signal on and a stop alongside the vehicle ahead of the space, about 2 feet away from it. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F35 | anchor: A06
Next, turn the wheel fully toward the side you are parking on, left for the left side of the road and right for the right side, and back up slowly. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F36 | anchor: A07
When your front door passes the rear bumper of the car you are parking behind, straighten the wheel and keep backing slowly in a straight line. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F37 | anchor: A07
Once your bumper clears the vehicle in front, turn the wheel sharply the other way and back slowly until you are parallel to the curb. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F38 | anchor: A07
Finish by straightening the wheels, ending about a foot from the curb and at least 2 feet from the vehicles ahead and behind. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F39 | anchor: A07
Let other drivers know where you are and what you intend by using headlights, brakes, turn signals and hazard lights, and by keeping space ahead and behind. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F40 | anchor: A07
Strong emotions affect safe driving, so do not drive when you are very worried, excited, afraid, angry or depressed. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F41 | anchor: A07
The horn exists to help prevent crashes: a light tap gets another driver's attention, and a hard press warns of a collision about to happen. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F42 | anchor: A08
Low beams help you see and be seen; even if your car switches them on automatically, learn the manual control and check that they come on when needed. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F43 | anchor: A08
Low beams are required when you cannot see a vehicle or person 500 feet away, about one block, and from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F44 | anchor: A08
Low beams are recommended whenever your windshield wipers are on and in rain, snow or fog. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F45 | anchor: A08
High beams let you see twice as far as low beams; use them when no vehicles are approaching or in an unfamiliar place or construction area, and dim them for oncoming traffic. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F46 | anchor: A08
If an oncoming driver leaves the high beams on, look toward the right side of the road, and use parking lights only while parked and idling. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F47 | anchor: A08
Turn on your signal, check around you, and then move; at an intersection, begin signaling about three seconds, roughly 100 feet, before the turn. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F48 | anchor: A08
When your turn comes just after an intersection, wait until you have crossed the intersection before signaling. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F49 | anchor: A08
Hand signals may replace turn signals that are missing or hard to see: arm straight out the driver window to turn left, elbow bent with the hand up to turn right, and hand pointed down to slow or stop. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0025]

Misconceptions: keeping the wheel turned while waiting to turn left is dangerous, because a rear-end hit would push you into oncoming traffic; a paved shoulder is not a passing lane except around a stopped or left-turning vehicle; mirrors and a backup camera are not enough when backing; missing an exit never justifies backing up; uphill with a curb is the one hill case where the wheels turn left.
Mnemonics: uphill with a curb, wheels left; every other hill case, wheels right; pass when both headlights show in the mirror; Y-turn is right, left, back, go; left arm straight for left, bent up for right, down for stop.
Glossary: U-turn means one continuous U-shaped turn reversing direction; Y-turn means a multi-step turnaround on a narrow street; blind spot means an area beside you that mirrors do not show; parallel parking means parking in line between two vehicles along the curb; low beams means normal headlights; high beams means brights; hazards means flashing warning lights.
Dynamic facts: whether a particular intersection allows a U-turn depends on local signs, so always check the posted signs where you drive.
